#comment: Portal `tumorType` free text to EFO / MONDO disease IRIs. Authored for demo 2,
#comment: whose indication hop needs `Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor` and
#comment: `Plexiform Neurofibroma` to reach a disease term. This is NOT the systematic
#comment: tumour-type mapping the phenotype-ontology work calls for -- it is its seed.
#comment:
#comment: Every mapped row was resolved by EXACT label match, case-folded, against the
#comment: disease terms of Open Targets Platform release 26.06 (which carries EFO, MONDO,
#comment: Orphanet, HP and NCIT), on the term name or an exactSynonym. Rows were not
#comment: hand-assigned, hence semapv:LexicalMatching. Matching against the terms the
#comment: indication data actually uses is deliberate: a mapping to a term that source
#comment: does not carry would satisfy a reviewer and still join to nothing.
#comment:
#comment: Values with NO exact match keep object_id sssom:NoTermFound and a note giving
#comment: the reason, rather than being dropped. Several are a base term plus a qualifier
#comment: (`Recurrent MPNST`, `Atypical MPNST`) where mapping to the base term would
#comment: silently discard the qualifier; several name a syndrome rather than a tumour.
#comment: `Cutaneous Neurofibroma` is the largest unmapped value and the first one worth a
#comment: curator's decision; its note names the candidate.
#comment:
#comment: Case variants map to the same term (`schwannoma` / `Schwannoma`), which is one
#comment: of the things this file is for.
#comment:
#comment: Rows are ordered by how many files carry the value, mapped rows first, so review
#comment: effort and file order agree.
